correctness.rationale: Checked source-to-offspring row convention and independent Poisson generating functions. Nonextinction is the largest fixed point of F(p)=1−exp(−τBp), obtained by iterating from one. For τρ(B)>1 a sufficiently small positive Perron vector multiple is a subsolution, guaranteeing positivity. Strict subhomogeneity of F excludes two positive fixed points by taking their maximum coordinate ratio; finiteness gives each coordinate strictly below one. With h(x)=−log(1−x)/x increasing, p_1>p_2 gives τr_1>h(p_1)>h(p_2)>τr_2 because each off-diagonal coefficient is positive; the other order is symmetric, and equality of coordinates forces equality of row sums, so all three signs are settled. value.rationale: The proof establishes the exact minimal dimension at which a simple total-offspring ranking ceases to be reliable and at which common scaling can change that ranking relative to the true nonextinction probabilities. The universal two-type classification and positive three-type witness jointly resolve a natural mathematical proxy question, not merely a numerical solution of one branching model. Conclusions are restricted to the abstract independent-Poisson nonextinction model, not outbreak sizes or calibrated predictions.
